correctness.rationale: Exact specialization of Skowron Definition 4 Eq. (6) is established from unit costs and binary approval; weak test follows his Theorem 1. The proof handles all n for k<=2 and all k for n<=2 (using nonempty elected support), and n=k=3, implying the sharp n+m>=8 lower bound. The two explicit weak-but-not-strong Pareto-efficient profiles are checked by hand. The boundary census enumerates all 1,470 and 10,200 distinct unlabeled-elected-candidate mask profiles, using exact integer denominators, all coalitions, and all voter permutations; it yields exactly five orbits, two PO. The included standalone verifier reproduces every finite count. Limitations: no generalization beyond full unit-cost approval committees.

originality.rationale: Skowron (2026, arXiv:2610.15516, Definition 4 and Example 4) already establishes the non-equivalence with 1,000 voters and twenty elected candidates. The new claim establishes a sharp voter-plus-candidate cutoff of eight, a complete five-orbit classification, and two Pareto-efficient minimal classes; these are not asserted in the inspected primary paper or its cited EJR+ foundations. Exact source statements and database hits were compared for implication, not only title resemblance. The possibility of unindexed or unpublished priority remains.
residual_risks: Semantic search not exhaustive over all independent publications, older equivalent concepts, inaccessible paywalled work, or author-private examples.
The result concerns the exact public 2026 strong EJR+ up-to-one form; changing the strict inequality or allowing unapproved elected projects can change the boundary.

value.rationale: Skowron’s published separation uses 1,000 voters with 20 elected candidates and motivates understanding structural/frequency differences. A sharp lower boundary, complete five-type census and two Pareto-efficient minimal mechanisms isolate the smallest genuinely nontrivial domain where that fairness distinction matters. This is a naturally motivated complete classification, not a routine restatement of the 1,000-voter example; its small exact census complements an all-size obstruction proof.
